paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness 的 SolidWorks MCP 集成（自本机仓库同步）
[](https://m8ven.ai/mcp/tan000tan-dsh-solidworks-1fp274?s=readme)# dsh-solidworks

DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts a local SolidWorks desktop behind 66 CAD tools
(parts, assemblies,

drawings, DFM, FEA). Read-only by default; document edits need a
higher policy tier and persistence
needs a one-shot user confirmation.

- Plugin package: `dsh-solidworks` — AGPL-3.0-only
- Execution engine: the `solidworks-automation-sk

ill` Python MCP server (MIT, vendored under `vendor/`, see `NOTICE`)
- Runtime shape: cordis plugin
inside the DSH host → spawns the Python MCP server over stdio → COM → `SolidWorks.exe`

Chinese documentation, including the full config and troubleshooting tables, lives in
README.zh.md.
## Requirements

Windows 10/11 x64 · SolidWorks desktop 2023–2026, activated and started at least once ·
Python 3.10+

x64 with `mcp>=1.27,<2`, `pydantic>=2`, `jsonschema>=4.20,<5`, plus `pywin32>=305`
and `comtypes>=1

.2` on Windows (`ezdxf`, `numpy`, `Pillow`, `lxml`, `openpyxl`, `python-docx`,
`python-pptx`, `XlsxW
riter` for the DFM/DXF/FEA families) · Node 22.12+.

The Microsoft Store `python.exe` alias cannot `import mcp`; discovery treats it as a failure
and nam

es every candidate it tried. Setting `pythonPath` to a real interpreter is the most
reliable configu

y candidate it tried. Setting `pythonPath` to a real interpreter is the most
reliable configuration.
## Install

- **Market**: install `dsh-solidworks` from the DSH market, then restart. No install script is
neede

d; all probing happens on first load (market installs block `postinstall` anyway).
- **Local tarball

**: `dsh plugin --profile web add .\dsh-solidworks-0.1.0.tgz`.
The `desktop` profile is owned by the

desktop app — use the GUI there. Keep the tarball on an
ASCII-only path: a non-ASCII directory make

s DSH record a garbled `file:` specifier.
- **Development**: add this directory to a profile's `cord

is.patch.yml` `insert` list (this repo
ships a ready `cordis.patch.yml`).

In a session, ask for `solidworks_status` first (it explains a broken environment), then
`solidworks

_connect`, then read-only calls such as `solidworks_mass_properties`.
High-risk calls require `solid
works_confirm` with byte-identical arguments, then the call itself.

The same policy is reachable from a terminal, which is the fastest way to tell "the plugin is
miscon
figured" apart from "the model asked for something silly":

## Policy
| `mode` | publishes | write calls | persistence calls |
| `read-only` (default) | 16 tools (health check, mass props, features, inspect sketch, mates, bound

ing box...) | refused | refused |
| `standard` | 42 tools (adds sketches, extrusions, cuts, revolves

, fillets, mates...) | allowed inside `allowedRoots` | refused |
| `full` | all 66 tools (adds save,
export STEP/STL/DXF/PDF, close, delete, Pack&Go;) | allowed inside `allowedRoots` | **needs one-sho
P/STL/DXF/PDF, close, delete, Pack&Go;) | allowed inside `allowedRoots` | **needs one-shot grant** |
A high-risk call without a matching grant returns:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The user (or an automation flow) approves it through the companion tool:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The grant binds to the SHA-256 of the canonical arguments, is single-use, and expires after five
min

utes (`grantTtlMs`). The session's current directory is the default write root when `allowedRoots`
i
s not set; any path outside those roots is refused even if the user confirmed it.

The list of shipped tools and their assigned tiers is in lib/policy.js; it was
verified against the
real Python MCP server at `tools/list` time (66 tools, zero drift).
## What happens when SolidWorks is missing or fails to launch
The host never crashes on startup:

- If Python is missing, or `server.py` cannot import `mcp`, or SolidWorks COM fails to register,
`ap

ply()` logs the diagnostic and publishes **only two meta tools**: `solidworks_status` and
`solidwork

s_confirm`.
- Calling `solidworks_status` returns structured JSON explaining what is missing (the ca

ndidate
interpreters tried, the missing COM classes, or the exit code) and the recommended next step

.
- The standard server tools stay unpublished until the environment is healthy — the model cannot
c

all tools that cannot run. Deployments that prefer the plugin registration to throw when CAD is
expe
cted to be present (e.g. a managed deployment) can opt in to `failOnStartupError: true` themselves.
## Verification status
`docs/verification.md` is the authoritative record; the short version:
- 110 assertions across seven suites pass: policy 11, MCP client 8, argument-shape 16, packaging 12,

audit trail 27, host-shaped end-to-end 27, crash isolation 9. Reproduce everything with
`$env:DSH_S

OLIDWORKS_PYTHON = "<python.exe>"; npm run test:all` (exit 0 = all green); `npm test`
runs the four

suites that need no Python (47 assertions).
- `tools/list` against the real Python server returns al

l 66 tools (protocol 2025-06-18); the
read-only tier publishes 16 + 2 meta tools and withholds the o

ther 50. The three modes were
measured against the live server: read-only 16, standard 42, full 66 p

ublished.
- The plugin loads in a real DSH host from an installed copy, spawns the vendored server,

serves
a real `solidworks_health_check`, survives `dsh plugin remove`, and leaves no orphan Python.

- **No modelling, assembly, drawing, save, or export call has been executed against a live
SolidWork

s session yet.** Write paths are gated and unit-tested, not proven. The minimal loop is
ready to run

the moment SolidWorks may be started:
`node tests/write-loop.mjs --python <python.exe> --authorised

` — new blank part → sketch +
[该节后续省略]
## 📜 Historical Architecture Note (Pre-0.1.0 Prototype)
The repository's earlier commit history (`8af9bef` to `d4c7fde`) includes an initial exploratory pro
totype exploring a C#-based SolidPilot execution service and custom DSH integration profiles.
In v0.1.0, the project transitioned to a standard npm-distributable DSH plugin architecture (`dsh-so
lidworks`), bundling the policy gate, FastMCP schema bridge, and audit logging into a single cohesiv
e package while keeping the full commit history preserved.
